author: Ankit
problem: Read a string S of '<', '=' and '>'. Print Yes if S is one '<', then one or more '=', then one '>', otherwise No.
bug_description: Only checks that S contains '<' and '=' and has as many '<' as '>', not their order, so strings like '>==<' get Yes.

comments.accurate: Checks that S is '<', then one or more '=', then '>'
comments.wrong_behavior: Accepts any string with '=' in it whose '<' and '>' arrowheads are balanced
comments.wrong_location: Arrow pattern check verified; check that the input is stripped of its newline

source.buggy_line: if "<" in S and "=" in S:
source.fixed_line: if "<" in S and "=" in S and ">" == S[-1]:
